tuning.note: The entities' numbers (docs/23a, D9; src/tuning.js has each one's meaning). These are the values the code carried until 2026-10-12, the cozy parent's for the most part, never re-decided: docs/02 question 19 is answered by editing this file. A section or a key left out keeps its default.

water.note: Unsafe water (Michael, 2026-10-19, #279): every natural source, water tiles and wells, is unsafe until purified, and its Drink says "(tainted)" (Michael, 2026-10-19). `clean` lists the sprites of sources that are safe (none yet; how water is purified is open); a waterskin's water is tainted unless its entry is marked `clean`.

stagger.note: a hit staggers the dead one with the weapon's staggerChance (this is the default), stopping its walk for the zombie's stagger seconds (data/tuning.json); after a stagger ends it cannot be staggered again for immunity seconds. Every landed hit shows a flinch whether or not it staggers, and any landed hit during a bite's wind-up cancels the bite (docs/41, step 1; the old `interrupts` field is retired). The cancel is a lever (Michael, 2026-10-23): what a cancelled bite costs the dead one (the bite's whole cooldown, zombie.cooldown in data/tuning.json; half of it the softer setting) and whether every hit cancels or only a staggering one are revisited after real combat testing, read by check("melee")'s lone-zombie row

bleed.note: a landed bite opens a wound with this chance, one more stack each (to max); the wound drains dpsByStacks[stacks - 1] a second, the timer is refreshed by each new bite and runs out by itself after duration seconds; a bandage stops it. Michael's bounds: five fresh stacks kill from full health in 10 s (not under 8 to 10 s), and one stack is a nuisance (under 5 health in all)

burn.note: burning (#14, Michael 2026-10-15): like bleeding but capped at one; a body burning loses dps a second for duration seconds, a new source refreshing the timer and never stacking, and never more than cap over one burn however often refreshed (Michael: never more than 10 against 100, the dead's health then; the cap is kept at 10 against 150 since docs/41 step 6, a number not a ratio, until Michael says otherwise). Only the dead burn, never a player. Sources: a weapon's `ignite` chance (the torch's 0.25 in data/items.json), the fireball and a fire arrow always (their `ignite`)

infection.note: a landed bite infects with this chance; the moodle goes green, yellow, orange, red over this many in-game days; it does nothing else yet (docs/02 question 29b)

combo.note: the third hit on one dead one within `window` seconds always floors it; switched off for testing (Michael, 2026-10-12), the code kept

finisher.note: what a blow on a downed dead one is multiplied by (was 2)

dual.note: an off-hand swing leaves you exposed for `window` seconds: a blow takes `front` times its damage from the front arc, `side` times from the sides, `behind` times (fatal) from behind; `lockout` is the share of a swing before the other hand may swing; `offDamage` multiplies the off hand's blows (1 = full; World of Warcraft's flat penalty would be 0.5) (docs/21)

blow.note: pointBlank: tiles this close are always hit; knockdownChance: the share of hits that floor the dead for a weapon with no knockdown of its own: 0 since docs/41 step 3 (was 0.3, 'high; for the combat pass'), so only a weapon with its own knockdown floors (the mace, the halberd's thrust, the shove); tiredDamage: a swing the bar cannot pay for (stamina below its cost; docs/41 step 4) lands at this share; hitStop, hitStopKill: seconds the world freezes on a hit and on a kill (0.07 and 0.12 since docs/41 step 1); swingMove: the walk's share while the swing's animation plays, the commitment to a swing (docs/41 step 1)

bow.note: the fireball as a flare (#156, Michael 2026-10-17): fireballGlow its light in flight, flareRadius and flareSeconds the light where it lands (light only), kindleRadius how near it lights a campfire or mounted torch; the bow's draw and every arrow's and thrown thing's flight (archery.js tunables; a bow's own drawTime, braceDrawTime, damage, and a thrown block override them): range and speed in tiles, heights in px; drawSpeed and braceMove the walk while drawing and braced; recoverTime the pause after a shot

shove.note: Space (docs/41 step 2): no damage, a push of knockback tiles (0.65 since 2026-10-24; a tired shove, one the bar cannot pay for, pushes tiredPush of it and staggers and floors at blow.tiredDamage, its stagger kept under cooldown so an empty bar holds no crowd), a stagger of stagger seconds, a knockdown by chance, on up to targets of the dead in the wedge whatever the Multi-hit setting; cooldown is also the recovery in which no swing starts

campfire.label: Campfire
campfire.note: docs/43 section 3 (Michael, 2026-10-25): built on open ground outdoors only, no skill and no tool; its two logs are its starting fuel, not materials (Take apart gives back half its stones)

hearth.label: Hearth
hearth.note: docs/43 section 4 (step 3): built inside a room, against a wall; a switch (section 3), out when built; no tool (the builder's default, as the campfire's)

looks.note: The character screen's palettes (docs/12, the creation screen; docs/31/03, the identity). The skin ramp is the design agent's, approved by Michael 2026-10-12 (data/art/character/character_body.json): eight living tones pale to deep, three dead ones (grey-green, grey, bruised blue) allowed in the creator for fun (Michael, 2026-10-13). The shadow is the engine's own rule (tone * 0.84). Hair and eye colours are first picks, Michael's to change here; a painted hair with no dye option (purple) keeps its own colours.

settings.note: "auto" or a number: how big the interface is drawn
the zoom: "auto" or one of view.ZOOM_LEVELS
the text in the top-left corner
on by default since 2026-10-15 (Michael: a sandbox setting, the dead hunt unless you turn them off); off they wander and ignore you (2026-10-10). A browser that saved its settings keeps its own
on: the dead hunt villagers, whatever aggro says; with aggro on, the player first when both are in sight (two knobs on purpose, Michael 2026-10-15; docs/19)
a bar at the bottom centre of the screen while a swing recovers (World of Warcraft's swing timer; docs/21)

the landing marker and dotted line while you draw a bow, wind up a throw, or cast (docs/20); on by default since 2026-10-24 (Michael, #385: "the little marker zipping down the line ... is like a loading bar"), off for the challenge; it was off from 2026-10-16. A browser that saved its settings keeps its own
outline the zombies the next swing would hit (docs/14): on by default since docs/41 step 1 (green means the swing lands)
on: a blow reaches everything in its wedge; off: only the nearest. Off is the intended way to play (Michael, 2026-10-12): multi-hit is the easy button (docs/14)
draw the dead's body samples, green when the next swing reaches them (docs/14)
on: building costs nothing (docs/13), for testing structures
the world has trees: the last choice at a Sandbox step (a world's own rule since #130; it replaced Combat testing's tree strip)
how many of the dead a world starts with, "none", "low", "standard" or "high": the last choice at a Sandbox step (#130)
on since docs/30 step 2 (hunger, thirst, tiredness drain); off: the body is a workbench
the player's hair (the character screen writes it, and `look.hairStyle` with it; kept for what reads it)

the look before docs/31/09 (skin, hair, eyes, hairStyle): migrated with playerName; identities.js keeps them now
another player's name over their head while in sight (docs/31/03)

stages.name: Bitten
stages.text: The bite broke the skin. You feel fine. Watch it.

stages.name: Fevered
stages.text: A chill and a headache. It is spreading.

stages.name: Sick
stages.text: Your hands shake. There is not much time.

stages.name: Turning
stages.text: It has taken hold. (Nothing happens yet: a marker.)

stages.name: Hungry
stages.text: Your stomach is making itself heard.

stages.name: Very hungry
stages.text: Hard to think about anything but food.

stages.name: Starving
stages.text: You are wasting away. Eat something.

stages.name: Parched
stages.text: Hard to catch your breath. Stamina recovers slowly.

stages.name: Dying of thirst
stages.text: You will not last long without water.
